title: MKT-03 CAC: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The CAC figure is produced under different accounting rules - cost divided by all customers, which understates acquisition cost by an order of magnitude - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is allocated marketing and partner cost; denominator is new valid customers acquired in the same period.
The dictionary entry for 'CAC' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: allocated marketing and partner cost divided by new valid customers in the window
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: cost divided by all customers, which understates acquisition cost by an order of magnitude
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: with no new customer in the window the metric is NOT_DEFINED rather than 0 TWD

steps.action: Compute CAC from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.marketing
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports 200 TWD and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute CAC independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value 200 TWD, and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports with no new customer in the window the metric is NOT_DEFINED rather than 0 TWD; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: CAC equals 200 TWD for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'allocated marketing and partner cost' and denominator scope 'new valid customers acquired in the same period'.

A recomputation that yields cost divided by all customers, which understates acquisition cost by an order of magnitude is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.
Boundary behaviour: with no new customer in the window the metric is NOT_DEFINED rather than 0 TWD; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Dividing by returning customers so acquisition looks cheaper.
Omitting partner or affiliate cost from the numerator.
evidence: Cost allocation extract with the allocated amounts.
New-customer list used as the denominator.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for MKT-03 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
